# 🤖 Copilot Instructions — Multi-Asset Trading Platform

## Purpose
Defines how developers and Copilot collaborate in this monorepo.  
Goal: leverage Copilot to accelerate code scaffolding **without compromising determinism, latency, or compliance**.

---

## 1. General rules
- Never accept Copilot code blindly — always **review, benchmark, and test**.
- Label generated sections:
  ```rust
  // GENERATED BY COPILOT — REVIEWED
Copilot output must always include:

Unit tests

Benchmark harness (for hot paths)

Example usage

2. Scope of Copilot use

✅ Allowed:

Data structure scaffolding (ring buffers, queues)

Serialization/deserialization helpers

Kafka producer/consumer wrappers

Integration tests

Schema generation (Avro/Protobuf)

UI code / dashboards

Deployment YAML templates

🚫 Disallowed:

Proprietary trading algorithms

Crypto key management

Regulatory reporting transformations

Manual data reconciliation without review

3. Recommended prompt format

Example:

// COPILOT: generate a lock-free ring buffer for order events in Rust.
// Requirements:
// - no heap allocation on push/pop
// - atomic head/tail counters
// - preallocated Vec<OrderEvent>
// - include unit tests and criterion benchmarks


or

// COPILOT: implement REST handler for /risk/check
// Must be deterministic, thread-safe, <2ms latency
// Include tests and example request/response

4. Developer workflow

Add descriptive comments above intended code.

Let Copilot generate a snippet.

Manually review logic, correctness, and latency behavior.

Mark generated section.

Run:

make lint test bench


Commit with message following Conventional Commits
:

feat(matching): implement SPSC queue using preallocated buffer

5. Review requirements

Every Copilot-assisted PR must:

Include tests

Include benchmarks (if hot-path)

Be reviewed by a senior engineer

Be traceable (commented // GENERATED BY COPILOT — REVIEWED)

6. Security & Compliance

Never include credentials or secrets in prompts.

Never paste raw client data into Copilot.

Copilot output must pass security scans (Bandit, Trivy, Sonar).

7. Example workflow summary
# Add file
touch services/matching/src/ring_buffer.rs

# Prompt Copilot
# COPILOT: generate SPSC ring buffer with atomic head/tail

# Review and mark
git add services/matching/src/ring_buffer.rs

# Run tests
cargo test --all
cargo bench --all

# Commit
git commit -m "feat(matching): add lock-free ring buffer [copilot-reviewed]"

8. Quick reminders

✅ Use Copilot for scaffolding
✅ Always test, benchmark, and lint
✅ Never use Copilot for crypto or regulation logic
✅ Review before merge
✅ Label AI-assisted sections
